# Spar 0.6.2

**Spar could already tell you something worth hearing — "you restored the
invariant on the first shrink and stopped" rather than "you're weak at sliding
window". What it could not do was remember it. 0.6.2 gives the fine-grained
finding somewhere to live, makes the number beside it answer to the evidence,
and picks the next problem by where you are rather than by a difficulty word.**

## The finding comes back

- **Your patterns are readable, so they can be confirmed.** Reading an ability
  now returns the mistake patterns filed under it and its recent behavioural
  evidence, searching the learner model searches all three, and the open
  patterns ride along in every turn unasked. A hypothesis written three attempts
  ago used to come back only if something happened to search the exact words it
  was filed under — so the same finding was written down twice instead of being
  promoted once.
- **A pattern still has to survive two attempts.** Unchanged, and now it can
  actually happen: the second sighting has something to match against.
- **Interpretation is required.** Every ability update carries at least one
  entry saying what you actually did. "Failed the window question" is a verdict
  and interprets nothing; the path that let the host fill one in from
  passed/failed is gone.

## The number answers to the evidence

- **Proficiency is a reading, not a count.** Three linked evidence items used to
  promote an ability to *independent* whether they were passes or failures. It
  is now polarity and strength, halved every 45 days, discounted where being
  helped would flatter the claim and never where it would not.
- **The judgement stays yours.** Status is still the agent's call — it has the
  replay, the code and the conversation. The evidence reading sits beside it as
  a second opinion, and when the two disagree Spar says so. That disagreement is
  the most interesting row in the ledger and it used to be unrepresentable.
- **Abilities go stale on their own.** Forty-five days without a check and an
  ability stops counting as current, without touching its version or its
  timestamp — nobody wrote anything, and a clock should not report progress.

## A rating you can lose

- **Glicko-2, against the challenge as an opponent.** The old number was a
  confidence-weighted mean of every ability's proficiency stretched onto a span.
  It could not fall on a failure, did not care how hard the challenge was, and
  moved when the agent rewrote a document on a day nobody solved anything.
- **Estimated on the Codeforces scale, because that is the scale the problems
  are on.** A Codeforces problem rating is defined as the rating at which a
  solver is even money against it, so a rated problem needs no translation to be
  used as an opponent. The Spar Rating is that number in Spar's own band; the
  LeetCode figure is the one real translation and says "~" because it is one.
- **A challenge Spar wrote is priced absolutely.** Pricing it against the
  learner made the rating a ratchet — fourteen solves of the same warm-up
  climbed from 1500 to 2700, because nothing in the loop was fixed.
- **Time away widens it.** A rating nobody has tested in months is less certain
  than it claims, so the first challenges back move it properly instead of being
  damped by a precision nobody re-earned.

## The next problem is chosen for you

- **The level rule is the rating now.** What the agent may set you was three
  buckets off a status word. It is the problem's own price against a window
  inverted out of the same curve that scores the result afterwards — so the gate
  that admits a problem and the rating that scores it cannot come to disagree.
- **The window follows the question.** Near even money to diagnose something
  untested, pitched against you to practise, a stretch to re-check something you
  have already shown. It widens on its own while your rating is provisional,
  because when Spar has not measured you yet more problems are plausibly right.
- **The agent is told the window.** It used to discover the rule from a
  refusal.
- **Spar's pick is a pick.** The problem library's leading suggestion ranks by
  how close a problem is to one you would solve about three times in five,
  instead of by whichever source answered first.

## Around it

- **One layout for a live challenge and a past one**, so stepping back through a
  session is travel rather than a reload.
- **A concept map over the problem library**, for the same library seen from
  above.
- **The type set in the platform's own face.**
